correctness.rationale: The exact published A4 generators produce a group of order 12, facet-orbit sizes 12/12/4, 28 facets, 42 edges and 48 graph triangles. A separate integer calculation from the inspected facet data independently gives Smith invariants 27 copies of 1 and one 2 for the 28 facial relation rows in a rank-31 graph-cycle lattice, hence H1 is Z^3 plus Z/2. I independently enumerated the 20 nonfacial triangles, checked the source explicit cocycle-coordinate vectors against all facial relations and the free generators/torsion witness, and obtained eight unoriented exact classes over four primitive free directions, each with lift multiplicities 1 and 4. The computed A4 action has carrier orbits of sizes 4,4,12. These are finite complete enumerations of the finite graph, not extrapolations to a family.
risk: The homology splitting into three free coordinates and one torsion bit is noncanonical; exact multiplicities and orbit relations, not coordinate labels, are the invariant content.
The result describes only simple edge cycles of minimum length in this one triangulation, not arbitrary metrics or longer cycles.

value.rationale: The exact primitive free-versus-torsion shortest-cycle shell is a natural invariant for a published highly symmetric small triangulation with both free and torsion H1. The nonuniform 4+1 lift multiplicities in every direction and separate A4 carrier/class orbits are mathematically interpretable structural features unavailable from f-vector or abstract homology, useful as a complete worked benchmark for integer systolic and equivariant finite-surface computations.
risk: Value is narrowly for a natural fixed triangulation; no claim about other genus-four surfaces or higher systolic lengths.
sources: Exact independent integer homology/carrier census and A4 orbit count

final_claim: On the Köhler--Lutz twelve-vertex vertex-transitive nonorientable genus-four surface, exactly twenty nonfacial triangular edge cycles realize the shortest nonzero integral homology classes; there are four primitive free directions, both order-two torsion lifts in each with multiplicities four and one, and specified A4 carrier/class orbits.
limitations: Noncanonical homology basis; statement concerns simple edge cycles and this specific complex.
Exact finite enumeration is exhaustive only because this graph has 12 vertices and all 3-sets were checked.
Unindexed prior finite-complex tables remain an originality risk.
